idiom_name: Node Permission Model (--permission with --allow-* grants and process.permission.drop) plus # private elements
implementation_notes: Node ships a grant model for the process itself. Started with --permission, access to the filesystem, the network, child processes, worker threads, native addons, WASI, FFI and the inspector is denied unless a flag grants it (--allow-fs-read=/srv/app, --allow-net, --allow-child-process), violations throw ERR_ACCESS_DENIED, process.permission.has(scope, reference) answers at runtime and process.permission.drop(scope) revokes a grant irreversibly for the rest of the process - the sanctioned shape of raise-late and drop-early, stable since Node 22.13 and 23.5. The documentation is equally explicit that this is a seat belt against trusted code rather than a sandbox against malicious code, so it belongs above an OS boundary, not instead of one. In-process, # private fields (ES2022) are enforced by the language rather than by convention, which lets a component be handed an object that cannot even name the state it must not touch. The classic rights-table object is justified only inside the application, where the grant set is business policy rather than process authority.
pitfalls: The permission model is documented as a seat belt, not a security boundary: malicious code can bypass it, so use it to bound accidents in trusted code and put untrusted code behind an OS sandbox or a separate process.

Grants are coarse when written for convenience: the entrypoint gets file read automatically, and a wildcard such as --allow-fs-read=/srv/* behaves as the whole directory, so a grant added for one file quietly authorizes everything beneath it.

drop() affects future checks only: descriptors, sockets, child processes and workers that were already opened keep working, so the application must close them itself before treating the drop as containment.
Workers and child processes do not inherit a narrowed authority automatically: each re-derives its own permissions, and a worker spawned before the drop keeps the ability to spawn more.
